reasoning: Alternative-lane research (newsletters, forums, short-interest and private-market data) plus the filings for base facts. Key findings: (1) Centrus has still not disclosed SWU capacity or total build cost (SMR.INTEL, Q1/Q2 calls); the only hard unit price is DOE's $17M/MTU HALEU option and $200/SWU spot. (2) On my estimates (~$1,450/SWU-yr capex, $200 real SWU, 45% margin) a greenfield initial phase roughly earns its cost of capital; value comes from the DOE $900M milestones, net cash and the option to scale. (3) The private mark for General Matter (~$2B pre-money, Mar 2026; three sources) is the best transaction anchor and supports ~$100/sh even after a 40% sector markdown. (4) Short interest ~30% of float (stockanalysis; up from 22% in July per GuruFocus/Equibles) and the 60-day lock-up end ~Nov 8 (424B5) shape the next month. (5) Dilution is first-order: 22.6M economic shares now, $1.7B capex after the horizon vs ~$500M net cash then, $1B ATM; I count a probability-weighted raise. Engine fair value $55.8 (DCF off: FY2028 NOPAT negative). For the ladder I do not put the median at my FV: the market and sell side ($240.82 avg) have more data on capacity, so I set scenarios bear $50 (0.35) / base $95 (0.45) / bull $190 (0.20) with 35-40% within-scenario vol, giving a median ~$87, mean ~$105, P(>= $109.88) 0.35. X/Twitter and Reddit were not reachable (blocked); no Polymarket/Kalshi market on Russian LEU waivers exists, so no market-implied probability entered. Research ~30 queries; Investor Day economics are the main unknown.

model_inputs.structure_note: Fuel-cycle developer in transition: the standard DCF cannot read FY2028 (Russian supply barred after 2027, own Piketon output only from 2029-30), so the engine sets the DCF to 0 (pre-profit year 3). Value is carried by (1) a SOTP (weight 0.40) with the Piketon LEU and HALEU programmes as rNPV parts (contract-book revenue x margin, phase probabilities, expansion capex and the DOE $900M milestone payments as dev costs) plus the unallocated transition burn as a cash-flow part; (2) three custom legs per method_fit: market-share scenarios (0.20), cash floor plus option (0.15) and General Matter transaction marks (0.15); (3) EV/sales 4.0x NTM as a capped cross-check (0.10). Leg weights are judgment, untested. The three-year segment build (FY2026-28) feeds only the EV/sales leg; expansion capex is kept out of the years and enters through net_debt_horizon (spend before H) and the rNPV dev costs (after H) so it is counted once.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (a) capex per SWU-yr ~$1,450 (total ~$2.6B from mid-2026 for ~1.3M SWU LEU + 12 MTU HALEU) is my estimate - Centrus has not disclosed SWU capacity or total cost; at ~$1,000/SWU (Orano/Urenco-like) the SOTP leg rises ~$15/sh and FV ~+$7/sh; (b) net_debt_horizon -500 and shares.horizon 24.83M are stated directly (derivations in inputs_detail) and include a probability-weighted $500M raise (p 0.4); (c) the 0% 2032 convert PV adjustment +$130M; (d) the DOE task order is modelled inside the HALEU rNPV, not in `contracts`, because its payments are tied to the build milestones that the rNPV probabilities already carry; (e) fair value $55.8 is far below spot ($109.88) and the sell-side average target ($240.82): the gap rests mainly on (a) and on SWU price/margin assumptions, flagged as low-to-medium confidence.
